newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms on exporters, interbank rises.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms on exporters, interbank rises.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed late on Friday but was range-bound in a quiet day which saw support by exporters counter weakness from destabilising rumours in the market, traders said.
The baht was quoted at 31.90/32.00 late on Friday onshore against 31.90/32.10 per dollar in the morning.
"I was a little surprised that the baht held up so well today as there was so many rumours in the market," said a trader at a large local bank.
"It was pretty soft today but everytime the baht dipped to 32 the exporters sold (dollars)," she said.
An unfounded report appearing on some traders' screens overnight suggesting a possible coup was being planned in Thailand rippled through the local market all day.
Thai military officials have repeatedly denied plans of a coup, saying they would not use force to solve the country's economic and political problems.
There was also talk of further finance company suspensions being planned next week, traders said.
"It's probably put about by someone with a long position," said one trader.
The one month baht/dollar swap premium rose to 16/21 satang per dollar against 15/20 in the morning.
The overnight interbank offered rate was quoted at 16-17 percent against 12-16 percent earlier and lending continued to be selective, dealers said.
